ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a set of inflorescence diagrams, with the bottoms labeled C, D, F, G, B, A, E respectively. The figure labeled G has an obvious main erect axis, and multiple lateral branches extend from the main axis; on these lateral branches, multiple small pedicels and flowers are distributed along the branches, presenting a “branched raceme” structure. The question asks for the term for “a branched flower cluster whose branches are racemes.” In botany, a compound or branched raceme is called a panicle.
